image.subject: A round-faced 12-year-old boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, eating a crisp red apple, leaning on a whitewashed picket fence on a dusty St. Petersburg street on a bright summer morning, a cheerful and gullible grin.

storyboard.claim: The gullible boys who paid Tom with apples and kites are the scene we laugh at.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben Rogers, apple in hand, at the fence in the sun.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the opening fence scene the book closes on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the exact boy the narrator means, so the reversal lands on a face.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression, standing by a whitewashed picket fence and looking at it as if seeing it for the first time, in soft afternoon light.

storyboard.claim: Maybe the boys who were conned were not fools after all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An adult pausing at the fence, rethinking it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the laugh of the previous line into a second look.
storyboard.addedInformation: A viewer sees the reader's own reassessment in the figure.

image.subject: Three barefoot boys in patched shirts line up at a whitewashed fence, handing over a kite, a tin bucket and a red apple to a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt who holds a whitewash brush and grins, a dusty street behind them in the morning sun.

storyboard.claim: The boys were paying for the privilege of an exclusive chance to take part.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys queuing to hand over treasures for a brush.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the boys were not fools, moving from doubt to a purchase.
storyboard.addedInformation: The barter is shown as an eager line, not a con.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt and patched knee trousers, barefoot, perched on top of a whitewashed picket fence and gazing down the dusty main street of St. Petersburg, a half-mischief grin on his face.

storyboard.claim: Tom understood the town better than anyone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom perched above the street, surveying the town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the boys to the boy who manages them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places Tom above the town, which fits the claim he read it best.

image.subject: A stack of pale Sunday school tickets fanned across a plain wooden schoolroom table beside a lit tallow candle, with a worn Bible at one end, in warm candlelit light.

storyboard.claim: Work, play and heroism are stories we agree to believe, not laws of nature.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tickets fanned on a table, worth only what the town agrees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the currency of the town's shared agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets carry the idea that value is agreed, not physical.

storyboard.claim: Value is a community agreement, and Tom was the master storyteller.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quotation card with the thesis line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Distills the previous beat into the book's thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: A real quotable line, so the text carries it without a picture.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat stands at a whitewashed picket fence on a sunlit street, watching a barefoot boy in a faded blue shirt with a whitewash brush paint the fence while the adult's hand rests on his own coat pocket, a thoughtful half-smile.

storyboard.claim: Consider Tom as you deal with your own week, office politics and chores.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grown adult watching a boy work the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the story toward the viewer's own week.
storyboard.addedInformation: The adult stands in for the viewer, watching the trick happen.

image.subject: A prosperous merchant in a black frock coat and white high collar counts gold coins at a polished wooden counter in a dim 1840s general store, a ledger open beside him and a lantern glowing on the shelf behind.

storyboard.claim: Tom is the prototype for the Gilded Age American businessman.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A merchant counting gold at a store counter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the businessman the narrator names a face.
storyboard.addedInformation: Period-correct props (gold, ledger, lantern) make the businessman concrete.

storyboard.claim: Tom was the original marketer, creating demand out of thin air.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A short punchline card, no picture needed.
storyboard.onScreenText: The original marketer: demand out of thin air.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens the businessman point into a single line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the trick plainly in a sentence the viewer can hold.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat stands in the open doorway of a plain clapboard house at dusk, looking out at a dusty street lined with whitewashed picket fences, the lamps just lit.

storyboard.claim: Look around your own life at the structures you buy into.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A doorway at dusk, looking out at the town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the thesis by asking the viewer to look at their own structures.
storyboard.addedInformation: The open doorway frames the viewer stepping out to look.
